tool: Invoicing: flat fee, hourly, contingency, hybrid
checked: Hourly: built from three known time entries (90m@35000=52500, 30m@35000=17500, 7m@33333=3889) plus a 1245c expense; subtotal/total/balance all 75134c to the cent and every source row got invoice_id set. Flat: milestone build gave exactly 125000c, the unpicked milestone stayed open. Contingency: 333333c, kind=contingency. Hybrid: milestone 100000 + time 18750 + expense 3333 + a -10000 discount line = 112083c, kind=hybrid. Edit removed a time line, recalculated to 93333c and released the TimeEntry back to unbilled. Void with a payment recorded is refused.
notes: FIXED. Quantity carries enough precision to multiply out to the printed amount, including on invoices built before the change. Totals unchanged. | Audit note: Time-line Qty is stored rounded to 2 decimals, so on short entries Qty x Rate does not equal Amount on the invoice, the PDF and the public page. The 7-minute entry prints as 0.12 x $333.33 = $38.89 (0.12 x 333.33 = $40.00). The total is right; only the printed line does not multiply out, which clients query.
repro: TimeEntry(minutes=7, rate_cents=33333) -> amount 3889c. Build an invoice from it: InvoiceLine.quantity = round(7/60, 2) = 0.12, unit_cents 33333, amount_cents 3889. GET /invoices/<id>/pdf shows '0.12  $333.33  $38.89'.

tool: Bulk invoicing and approval workflow
checked: Bulk: two matters each with a 120m@30000 entry; POST /invoices/bulk built exactly two drafts of 60000c each and consumed the entries. tool: Split billing across payers
checked: Matter with payers 60/40 and one 100001c time entry: two invoices of 60001c and 40000c, summing to exactly 100001c with the rounding remainder on the last payer; the first invoice carries time_entry_id, the second's copied line has it NULL. tool: Interest on overdue balances

POST /invoices/<id>/interest added exactly one line of 501c (50134 * 0.12 / 12, half-up), set interest_cents=501, last_interest_on=today and total 75635c. tool: Trust (IOLTA) accounting with three-way reconciliation
checked: Apply: /trust/apply moved 25000c together across all three places (invoice paid_cents 25000 / balance 50134, TrustTransaction type=to_operating -25000, Payment method=trust account=operating, client and matter balances both 500000 -> 475000). Overdraw: a 99999.00 disbursement was refused with a message and TrustTransaction.count() was unchanged; a disbursement taking the balance to exactly zero was allowed. Reconciliation: with one uncleared 100000c deposit in transit and 500000c of uncleared disbursements, a 500000c bank statement gave balanced=true with book=ledgers=100000; a 4900.00 statement gave balanced=false and reported the difference as -10000c on the report page. Then tested funds earmarked to one matter.
notes: FIXED. A matter may now spend only its own earmarked funds plus the client's unallocated balance; a draw spanning both writes one ledger row per source against a single payment. Over-allocated clients are flagged on /trust/ and the ledger. | Audit note: Trust funds held for one matter are silently spent on another matter's invoice. /trust/apply picks its source with `if matter_bal > 0`; when the invoice's matter holds nothing it falls through to the pooled client balance and writes the withdrawal with matter_id=None, even when the whole client balance is earmarked to a different matter. The other matter's sub-ledger keeps showing the full amount while the client no longer has it. Nothing refuses it and nothing warns: /trust/ only flags balances below zero, /trust/ledger/<id> shows the negative unallocated figure without comment, and because book and client ledgers move together the three-way reconciliation still reports balanced. This is the shortfall a bar audit looks for.
repro: One client, two matters. TrustTransaction(client_id=C, matter_id=A, type=deposit, amount_cents=100000). Sent invoice for 80000c on matter B. POST /trust/apply {invoice_id: B-invoice, amount: 800.00} succeeds. After: invoice paid 80000, matter A trust balance still 100000, client trust balance 20000, so the matter ledgers exceed the client balance by 80000c. GET /trust/ and /trust/ledger/<C> show no warning; a reconciliation for the period still returns balanced=true.

tool: Evergreen retainer top-up requests
checked: Matter with trust_minimum 500000 and replenish_to 750000 holding 250000: evergreen_shortfalls() returned exactly that matter with shortfall 500000 (replenish_to minus balance). `run_evergreen()` sent one request, wrote one AuditLog action=evergreen_sent for the matter, and a second immediate run sent nothing (14-day window). The email in the dev outbox asks for $5,000.00 with the firm's check and mailing instructions, which is the correct degraded path with STRIPE_SECRET_KEY blank.

tool: UTBMS codes and LEDES 1998B export
checked: UTBMS: /time/new and /time/expenses/new save task_code L120, activity_code A102 and expense_code E112, and reject codes outside the set (ZZZZ, QQ stored as ''). LEDES refusal: with no ids set, /exports/ledes returns 400 and names the missing LAW_FIRM_ID, the client and the matter. After setting them the export returns 200, line 1 is exactly `LEDES1998B[]`, line 2 is the 24-field header ending `[]`, and every data line ends `[]` and splits into exactly 24 pipe-separated fields with LAW_FIRM_ID and the client id populated. ledes_exported_at was stamped on every exported invoice. Then summed the line items against the header total.
notes: FIXED. Every line type is now emitted (fees as F, expenses as E, interest and adjustments as IF), so records sum to INVOICE_TOTAL, and the export refuses to write an unbalanced file. | Audit note: Interest lines are dropped from the file but are still inside INVOICE_TOTAL, so the record lines do not sum to the invoice total and an e-billing validator will bounce the file. invoice_lines() only yields kind in ('time','expense'); adjustment/discount/flat lines are dropped the same way, but only interest also inflates the header total. Separate caveat, not a failure: field 4 LAW_FIRM_MATTER_ID is filled with Matter.number and field 24 CLIENT_MATTER_ID with Matter.ledes_matter_id, which is a defensible but not the only reading of the spec.
repro: Invoice INV-1001 (three time lines 52500+17500+3889, one expense 1245, one interest line 501) -> total 75635c. GET /exports/ledes?from=2026-01-01&to=2026-12-31: every record carries INVOICE_TOTAL 756.35 but the LINE_ITEM_TOTAL column (field 13) over that invoice's records sums to 751.34.

tool: Multi-currency matters and invoices
checked: Matter with currency GBP: the built invoice copied currency='GBP'. Staff invoice detail, the invoice list and the invoice PDF all render GBP correctly (£400.00, plus a 'Currency: GBP' line on the PDF), and the outbound invoice email uses fmt_money. Then checked the two client-facing pages and the Stripe call.
notes: FIXED. Client-facing pages format in the invoice currency and name it once. A non-USD invoice cannot be charged in dollars: the pay button is withheld and a direct POST is refused. | Audit note: The client-facing pages ignore the invoice currency. app/templates/invoices/public.html formats every amount with the `|money` filter (USD only), never `|cur(inv.currency)`, and there is no currency note on the page, so a GBP invoice is shown to the client as $400.00. The pay confirm page (payments/pay_confirm.html) does the same, including the surcharge line. Separately, /pay/<token> always builds the Checkout Session with currency 'usd', so a GBP invoice paid online charges USD; the phase-2 contract calls Stripe out of scope, but combined with the '$' on the page the client is given no way to tell.
repro: Create a matter with currency='GBP', build and send an invoice of 40000c. GET /p/<public_token>: the page shows $400.00 with no mention of GBP. GET /pay/<public_token>?method=card: shows $400.00 + $12.00 surcharge = $412.00. GET /invoices/<id>/pdf correctly shows £400.00 for the same invoice.

tool: Client statement: every invoice, payment and trust application with a running balance

tool: Invoice template editor: logo, colour, columns, labels, payment wording, preview
checked: Saved a template that hides the Rate column and relabels bill_to/matter/invoice_number/due/balance_due, with a custom accent and title. The PDF dropped the Rate column and used 'STATEMENT OF ACCOUNT', 'Bill no', 'Payable by', 'Invoice to' and 'Amount now owing'; the public page at /p/<token> showed the same column set (Date, Description, Qty, Amount) and the same labels. Preview returns a SAMPLE PDF. Then turned on the timekeeper and UTBMS-code options the same editor offers.
notes: FIXED. The timekeeper lookup no longer assumes a relationship that does not exist, so the PDF and public page render with those columns on. A PDF failure now blocks the send instead of being swallowed. | Audit note: Ticking 'show timekeeper initials' or 'show UTBMS codes' (or adding the Timekeeper or Code column) makes the invoice PDF and the public invoice page return 500 for any invoice containing an expense line whose Expense has a user_id. app/blueprints/invoices.py:187 in line_meta does `_initials(e.user)` but the Expense model has user_id and no `user` relationship, so it raises AttributeError. The staff invoice detail page still renders and /invoices/<id>/remind still returns 200 (the send path swallows the PDF error and logs a warning), so the firm sees the invoice go out while the client gets an email with no PDF attached and a 'View and pay' link to a 500 page.
repro: Seeded data already has Expense id 1 with user_id 1. POST /settings/invoice-template with invoice_show_timekeeper=1 and the default columns. Then GET /invoices/1/pdf -> 500 and GET /p/<INV-1001 public_token> -> 500, both AttributeError: 'Expense' object has no attribute 'user' (app/blueprints/invoices.py:187, reached from line_description at :195). Untick the option and both return 200 again.

notes: FIXED. Same root cause as the template editor. tool: Stripe Checkout with idempotent webhooks
checked: app.blueprints._stripe monkeypatched. checkout.session.completed with amount_total 103001 and surcharge_cents 3000 created one Payment of 100001c with surcharge_cents 3000 and stripe_fee_cents 275 from the balance-transaction lookup, and moved the invoice to paid with balance 0. tool: Card on file with client consent (emailed link or from the portal), stored at Stripe
checked: POST /money/cards/<id>/request minted a 7-day PortalToken and emailed the consent link. GET /pay/card/<token> renders the consent page; POSTing without the tick box returns 400 and starts nothing; with the tick box it creates the Stripe customer and a setup-mode session and redirects 303. The success callback stored stripe_payment_method_id, card_brand=visa, card_last4=4242, card_authorised_on and marked the token used. Removing the card clears the four fields and turns auto_charge off on active plans. With STRIPE_SECRET_KEY blank the request route refuses with the not-configured message.
notes: Card capture itself happens on Stripe's hosted page; verified through monkeypatched _stripe.create_setup_session / retrieve_setup_session rather than a live account.

tool: Charge an invoice to the card on file, surcharge per firm settings
checked: Surcharge on (300bps): charging 100001c called Stripe for 103001c while the recorded Payment was amount_cents 100001 with surcharge_cents 3000 and stripe_fee_cents 320, and the invoice paid_cents moved by 100001 only (status paid, balance 0). Surcharge off: charging a 50000c invoice called Stripe for 50000c and recorded amount 50000 / surcharge 0. tool: Payment plans: weekly, biweekly or monthly installments, auto-charged or emailed (python -m app.cli payment_plans)

tool: Time, expenses, invoices, trust in one place
checked: Walked one matter end to end in a single app: logged time (timer and manual), added an expense with a receipt, built an invoice from both and confirmed the totals to the cent, sent it, applied trust and recorded a card payment, and saw the same numbers agree across /time, /time/expenses, /invoices, /trust/, /statements and /reports/wip.
